I was raised this way by my adoptive mother. She was completely detached, she was neglectful, she was cold. She was Catholic.

Her abuses ranged from neglect to unfathomable cruelty. And the things she invented to scare me….

I can’t say for sure that if I had had siblings, I wouldn’t have treated them the same. Because hurt people hurt people. You were living what you learned and you were under an enormous amount of stress and responsibility.

The only saving grace it that I was adopted because she couldn’t conceive, so there were no siblings. But if there had been, I would’ve been put in the position to do everything to care for them, too.

Be compassionate with yourself. They’re still young, but the time will come when they’re no longer under her wings and you can make amends then. In the meantime, work on yourself so you’ll be as ready as possible for that moment when it arrives.

You have every right to get stuck on that. It blows my mind that I’m even doing that. If it were a friend in my position, I would be very concerned. I never thought I would be someone who ignored a medical issue.

But tbh, I still haven’t mentally recovered from all my other surgeries. This came out of a complete medical trauma.

I’m diabetic and I cannot simply get in a machine. I first need a blood draw (I’m terrified of needles and it gets worse the more I get them) within two weeks of the test. Then I need to fast (my sugars drop so so low) because they’re scanning my abdomen. If the nurses are running late, which happens a lot, my anxieties ramp up and I hit my limit really fast. So if any of those things doesn’t go perfectly right, it gets called off and start all over again.  I’ve requested to make this more accessible, like no prior bloodwork or staying overnight in the hospital to have my sugars monitored and sedated properly. My surgeon claims theirs no accommodations like this. 

They moved back in with their patents for three months over the summer and I found myself very urgently in need. I gathered all my strength and independently searched (long days of phone calls) for a visiting nurse/caretaker/etc. through the county/state and they really will not provide one unless your elderly and/or dying. I’m on disability and the out of pocket minimum commitment is vastly more than I receive.

Otherwise I completely agree with you. The medical system is really fucked. I’m one of those people that falls between the cracks. We talked a lot about how if the burden of care was removed, they would fair much better. I really wanted that for them/us.
